traits.stem_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Mammillaria: Mammillaria: stems unsegmented, green to gray-green, spheric to cylindric or turbinate, often flat-topped, 1-15(-25) × 1.8-12(-20) cm; tubercles distinct, not confluent into ribs, pyramidal, conic, or cylindric, 3-25 × 2-9 mm; areoles of 2 kinds: vegetative areoles (spine clusters) at tips of tubercles; reproductive areoles in axils of tubercles, woolly, bristly, or naked. Flowers diurnal, in ring distant from stem apex (or nearly apical at anthesis forming a ring around new growth, subsequent apical growth displacing fruits even farther away from apex), in axils of tubercles, unconnected to spine clusters, funnelform, campanulate, or rotate; ovary lacking scales and spines. Fruits indehiscent, usually pink, bright red, or greenish, scales and spines absent (or rudimentary).
